claims.statement: Expects e-commerce industry growth of 15-20% and plans internal operations for that range
Expects FY25 capex to decline to 6.6-6.9% of revenue from 7.4% in FY24
Sufficient capacity to grow through FY25; only major addition is Bangalore mega facility; Tauru gateway capacity expanded 10-15% via process improvements
Express Parcel service EBITDA at 18.4% for FY24, in line with long-term 18-20% target; PTL incremental margins 40-50%; SCS service EBITDA doubled to 6.8%
Express Parcel volumes grew 12% YoY to 740M in FY24; PTL freight grew 30% YoY to 1.4M metric tons; Truckload grew 40% YoY
Express Parcel margins expected to remain in 18-20% range; PTL margins expected to reach Express-like levels over time
Overall service EBITDA margin improved to 11.9% (+1.7% Y-o-Y, +40bps Q-o-Q); Express Parcel stable at 18%; PTL improved to 3.2%
SCS pipeline robust across auto, electricals, FMCG; integrated fulfillment for e-commerce demand rising significantly
Expect Express Parcel service EBITDA margins in 17%-18% range going forward
Express Parcel service EBITDA margin 15.1% in Q2 FY25 vs 18.2% in Q1 FY25 due to peak season capacity investments
PTL service EBITDA margin stable at ~3% in Q2 FY25
Supply chain services service EBITDA negative Rs. 9 crores in Q2 FY25 due to one-time provision
Trucking CapEx at 2%-2.1% of revenue in FY25, tapering to 1%-1.1% in FY26 after steady-state tractor trailer penetration
SME volumes up ~50% YoY; D2C volumes up ~20% YoY excluding captive marketplace clients
Infrastructure grew to 19.49M sq ft in Q2 FY25 including 0.5M sq ft short-term peak season leases; gateways stable at 278; ASCs up from 42 to 45; parcel sorters 61 to 66
Team size grew from 67,900 to 73,800; fleet size from 15,800 to 16,400 in preparation for peak season
PTL margins expected to mirror Express Parcel margins (16%-17%) as volumes scale; currently at 3% from -20%
PTL service EBITDA margin target of 15%-16% does not include yield improvements; yield gains would be additional
Express Parcel structural margins unchanged at 16%-20.6% service EBITDA despite competitive pricing
Incremental capacity investments focused on PTL and heavy goods growth, not Express Parcel
Third-party quick commerce pilot launching in Bangalore with 2,500-5,000 sq ft in-city warehouses across 6-7 cities
Express Parcel steady-state service EBITDA margin target 17-20%
PTL revenue growth target 25-30% for next financial year
Capex as percentage of revenue expected to be 5.6% or lower this year, long-term target 3.5-4%
Rapid commerce revenue expected Rs 80-100 crore through the financial year
Express Parcel service EBITDA margin improved QoQ from 15.1% to 15.6% but depressed YoY due to fixed cost buildup and fleet cost inflation
PTL service EBITDA margin improved to 3.8%, highest in 11 quarters, with sequential improvement expected to continue
Corporate overheads flat for 11 quarters at Rs 211 crore (8.9% of revenue), glide path toward 6% continues
PTL December volumes highest since Spoton integration at ~147,000 tons; January continued strongly
HPCL partnership starting, will bring significant volume to PTL network
Capex as percentage of revenue 5.6% or lower this year, declining YoY; no major capex planned for next year, only routine hub upgrades

Infrastructure at 20.6 million sq ft including 0.5 million sq ft temporary peak season capacity; 112 major gateways/hubs, 45 automated sort centers with 65 sorters; sufficient capacity in network, utilization expected to rise next year
Fleet costs spiked in first week of October due to intra-city vehicle shortage; shifting to fixed contracts for next year
Capex intensity target of 3.5-4% of revenue long-term; FY25 Capex at 5.2% of revenue
FY27 Capex expected to hit 4% range due to Ecom Express automation assets reducing need for new parcel sortation systems
PTL service EBITDA margin expanded 700bps QoQ to 10.8% in Q4 FY25 driven by yield improvement, operating leverage, fleet utilization
Express Parcel service EBITDA margin 15.9% in Q4 FY25 vs 15.6% in Q3; FY25 margin 16.2% vs 18.4% in FY24 due to pricing overhang
Expect Express Parcel margins to expand in FY26 and beyond as pricing overhang clears and Ecom Express volumes integrate
PTL tonnage grew 19.4% YoY and 11% QoQ to 460,000 tons in Q4 FY25; FY25 tonnage 1.7M tons, up 18.7% YoY
Express Parcel volumes flat YoY at 177M packages in Q4 FY25; FY25 volumes 752M, flat YoY but up 90M vs FY23
Fleet utilization improved from ~65% pre-Q3 to >70% in Q4 FY25; definition of capacity changing due to better routing, loading, software
Real estate reduced from 20.5M to 20.1M sq ft QoQ; gateways constant at 111, automated sort centers at 45, sorters at 65
Express Parcel service EBITDA margin expected to remain within 16-18% normative range
PTL service EBITDA margin target of 16-18% expected at 600,000-640,000 tonnes quarterly load
Supply Chain Services revenue target of Rs. 1,800-2,000 crores in three years (FY29)
Ecom Express integration costs limited to Rs. 300 crores envelope, no further recurring costs expected
Overall service EBITDA margin expanded to 13% in Q1FY26, up 60bps QoQ and 190bps YoY
Express Parcel service EBITDA margin at 16.3% in Q1FY26, up from 15.1% low point in Q2FY25
PTL service EBITDA margin at 10.7% in Q1FY26, expected to rise with network utilisation improvements
Supply Chain Services margin improved significantly from 2.2% in FY25 to 7.2% in Q1FY26
PAT margin expanded to nearly 4% in Q1FY26 from 2.4% in Q1FY25, expected to continue expanding through FY26
Supply Chain Services pipeline at Rs. 300 crores in advanced conversion stages, over Rs. 1,000 crores total pipeline
claims.value: Rs. 300 crores advanced, Rs. 1,000+ crores total

claims.statement: Infrastructure at 20.4 million sq ft across 119 gateways, 45 automated sort centres, 64 sorters; mild expansion in freight network to 125 service centres
Express delivery centres to expand from 4,500 to 4,750-4,800 by end of FY26
Ecom Express network integration complete, 7 facilities to be retained, non-express businesses to exit by Q3FY26
PTL business targets 20% annual revenue growth for FY26, with Q1 at 17% YoY (higher adjusted for IndAS).
Ecom acquisition front-loads ~Rs 300 crore capex for sorting equipment, to be warehoused and deployed as long-term capacity needs arise.
Distribution centres grew 1% (4,450 to 4,500) while volumes rose 14% QoQ, implying 14% higher DC utilisation; sort centre utilisation also up 14% with flat count.
Line-haul tractor-trailer utilisation broadly 60-65%; marginal decline in Q1 due to fleet expansion and double-trailer experiments.
Delhivery handled 208 million packages in Q1 FY26 vs 180 million in Q4 FY25; July volumes significantly higher.
Incremental margins on Ecom volumes could exceed 35-40% as network utilisation rises 30-40% with only 6% DC expansion; last-mile fixed costs ~10% of total.
PTL margin path to high-teens supported by yield improvement from retail customer mix shift and existing customers becoming more quality-conscious.
Express parcel service EBITDA margin target 16-18% by end of 2026; margins can inch beyond 18% over time
Ecom Express integration costs materially lower than Rs 300 crore envelope; bulk within FY26
Express market growth expected at 15-20%; Delhivery to grow beyond market growth
PTL volume growth target ~20% for FY26; H1 at 15%, strong October and Q4 expected
Q2 FY26 service EBITDA margin 13.2% vs 9.3% YoY; express parcel margin 15.3% stable YoY
PTL margin 8.5% in Q2; H1 FY26 PTL margin Rs 100 crore equals full year FY25
Supply chain services margin improved to 12.8% in Q2 from -4.4% YoY; structural improvement via ops, tech, TMS integration
Express parcel shipments 246M in Q2 (+32.5% YoY, +18% QoQ); PTL tonnage 477K (+12% YoY)
Peak dispatch record 7.2M orders in a single day during festive period; crossed 100M transportation orders in September and October
H1 FY26 capex intensity 5.1% vs 6.6% YoY; trending toward long-term 4% target
Infrastructure expanded to 22.05M sq ft; 123 gateways, 50 automated centers, 74 sorters, 141 freight service centers, 160 processing centers, ~4,600-4,700 delivery/partner centers
PTL service EBITDA margin target of 16-18% in next 24 months not dependent solely on 20% growth
Express service EBITDA margin for September-October combined will be higher than 15.3%
Adjusted EBITDA margins typically improve in H2 due to better sweating of fixed assets added in H1
Ecom Express integration cost of Rs 90 crore in Q2 and additional Rs 100 crore over next two quarters
Rapid Commerce and Delhivery Direct total investment currently about Rs 15 crore
Rapid Commerce live in 20 dark stores across 3 cities, launching in Delhi NCR and Mumbai by Q4
Delhivery Direct live in 3 cities, expanding to 5 more by end of FY26
Ecom integration total cost envelope expected significantly below original Rs 300 crore estimate
Crossed milestone of ₹1,000 Cr service EBITDA in a FY for the first time
Q3 FY26 Service EBITDA reached Rs 421 crore at 15.1% margin; Express margin at 18.1%, PTL at 11%, SCS improved to 13% from 2.1% YoY.
9M FY26 Service EBITDA crossed Rs 1,000 crore milestone for the first time.
Adjusted EBITDA for Q3 FY26 was Rs 147 crore, nearly matching full FY25 Adjusted EBITDA.
PAT before Ecom integration costs was Rs 110 crore (3.8%); after integration costs Rs 40 crore.
Express network has stably operated at 22-23% margins historically; management sees no reason margins cannot rise if pricing holds, but cautions service quality may suffer beyond that range.
Capex expected to decline to 4-4.4% of revenue over medium term (7-10 quarters); near-term phasing may shift between quarters but trajectory unchanged.
New business investments (Delhivery Direct, rapid commerce) estimated at Rs 60-80 crore for next fiscal year; Delhivery International profitable from launch.
SCS has a healthy pipeline and clear plan to accelerate top-line growth after margin-focused restructuring; new mandates starting implementation this quarter.

Mid-mile capex driven by PTL, not e-commerce; vehicle-related capex (LNG trucks, tractor-trailers) and potential sixth mega gateway in Noida (not imminent); sorter capex minimal as equipment acquired via Ecom Express.
PTL salesforce expanded to ~60 locations from 6 major ones two quarters ago; new teams fully trained and on ground, expected to accelerate new client acquisition in Q4 FY26 and FY27.
Network utilization higher across facilities and haulage; technology-driven productivity gains (e.g., auto-docking saving 20-30 mins per truck) contributing to margin expansion.
Free cash flow breakeven expected at ~6% Adjusted EBITDA margin; CapEx steady state ~4.5% of revenue; working capital at 15 days
PTL volume growth guidance of 15-20% long-term average; near-term quarters may vary 17-23%
Corporate overheads expected to settle in 6-7% of revenue range from current 9.1%
Service EBITDA margin target 16-18% over next three years; corporate costs to ~7%; overall Adjusted EBITDA 10-11%
ROIC target 25-30% on tangible assets (ex-cash, ex-ROU) at steady state
CapEx as % of revenue not increasing; decline may be slower due to earlier vehicular capex (LNG trucks/tractor trains) for anticipated volumes
Express CapEx not significant; Ecom Express sorters being deployed; PTL facility relocations only
PTL margins to continue improving with volume; Q3 margin ~11% suppressed by excess infrastructure built early for e-commerce peak
Supply Chain Services margins at 13% with no cap; accounts delivering 30%+ EBITDA; potential to improve via inventory reduction for clients
Express parcel margin levers: DC utilization (800 to 1,100 pkgs/day), infrastructure consolidation (Pune, Delhi NCR), claim rate reduction (30-40 bps), D2C heavy volume growth, dynamic pricing
DC capacity utilization rising: currently ~800 pkgs/day per DC vs theoretical ~1,100; sorters and infrastructure consolidation to add margin
Intermediate Processing Centres
Return Processing Centres
FY26 Capex as % of revenue 4.7%
~₹1,800 Cr pipeline of annual business potential under active discussions
Free cash flow turned positive at Rs 89 crore in FY26, one year ahead of plan
CapEx intensity target of 4% of revenue; currently at 4.7% and motoring ahead of plan
Investment of Rs 130-160 crore planned for new initiatives in FY27
Express business at upper end of normative margin guidance of 16-18%
PTL margins expanded successively; capital intensity reduced to less than 5% of revenue
Supply chain services service EBITDA expanded 4x to Rs 79 crore at 10.9% margin
Transport adjusted EBITDA expanded 260 bps to 6.3% for FY26
Overall adjusted EBITDA margin at 4.4% for FY26 (Rs 457 crore on Rs 10,486 crore revenue)
Core transport ROIC reached 16%, up from 5.2% earlier
Steady-state transport ROIC potential of 25%+ driven by EBITDA margin expansion to 10%+ and capital intensity improvement
Delivered over 1 billion packages in FY26; 306 million in Q4 FY26 with sequential growth
PTL volume reached 2 million metric tons in FY26; 549k metric tons in Q4 FY26 with 20% YoY growth
Supply chain services signed and activated two mandates in Q4 FY26; pipeline healthy
CapEx as percentage of revenue reduced from 7.8% in FY23 to 4.7% in FY26
AGV pilots in Bombay mega gateway ready to scale; expansion to other mega gateways within FY27
Tractor trailer count increased QoQ; vendor fleet mix shifted toward per-kilo model
Express volume growth tracking towards upper end of 20-30% YoY range for FY27
Automation investments in transportation facilities and fulfilment centres (in-facility movement, ASRS) brought forward to sustain market share growth amid labor shortages
Express service EBITDA margin target 16-18% for FY27, confident to reach higher end in H2
PTL service EBITDA margin target to exit FY27 at 15-15.5%, up from 13.4% exit FY26
Q1 FY27 normalized EBITDA impact from fuel and wage inflation estimated at 35 Cr, with 30-35 Cr delay in fuel pass-through to Q2
Two large new supply chain services contracts (industrials and consumer durables) in ramp-up phase causing temporary margin drag
Supply chain services new contracts expected to reach full margin potential 45-60 days after inventory roll-in
New initiatives investment budget 160-175 Cr for FY27, mostly for Delhivery Local; financial services just received NBFC approval in July
Network structural changes as freight service centers activated: heavy loads withdrawn to gateways, reducing average delivery center size and costs
Business development teams expanded for part-truck and full-truck freight across 100 cities, increasing wage costs in Q1 FY27.
Corporate overheads stable at ~9.3-9.4% of sales in FY25, FY26, and Q1 FY27; operating leverage not yet visible.
Contractual manpower expense rose to 12.8% of revenue in Q1 FY27 from 12.2% a year ago, impacting EBITDA margin by ~0.6%.
Fuel and oil-price linked costs (linehaul, consumables, air movement, last-mile partner payouts) increased materially in Q1 FY27.
Annual increments and network expansion in H1 FY27 increased fixed cost base.
Delhivery Local (new services) contribution margin significantly ahead of plan in Q1 FY27; expected to improve further in Q2 and Q3.
Cash integration cost for Ecom Express at 17 Cr in Q1 FY27; total cash guidance 300 Cr.
Heavy freight loads (>200 kg) withdrawn from forward service stations into gateways, reducing average service centre size and rental, supervisory, and storage costs.
Capex as % of revenue 3.7% in H1FY27
Express volume growth for FY27 expected at upper end of 20-30% range, potentially beyond
Express service EBITDA margin for FY27 expected around 17%
Aggregated transportation margins to expand 130-150 bps YoY in FY27
E-commerce volume growth guidance of 15-20% for FY27 remains reasonable
PTL margins to expand YoY in FY27
Express margins at least equal to FY26 levels, with potential upside from PTL volume growth
Investing in automation (AGVs, robotics) and AI initiatives; 40% stake in Falcon Autotech gives cost curve visibility
FY27 EBITDA loss guidance Rs 130-160 Cr; H1 loss Rs 67 Cr tracking at lower end; FY28 loss expected broadly in same range unless contribution margins improve further.
Supply chain services pipeline remains robust; two new Q1 businesses stabilised and expanding; e-commerce starts up 50%+ YoY; enterprise side conservative due to cost unpredictability.
PTL TAM estimated at Rs 90,000-100,000 Cr (5x Rs 15-20k Cr organised market) driven by unorganised segment, migration from slow to fast PTL, and FTL-to-PTL shift.
